words.prose: {{ar:عِيشَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:'īshatin}}) is the life-state into which the evaluated person is placed. Grammatically it is genitive under {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), so it is the domain of the predicate rather than the actor of the whole clause. Its feminine genitive indefiniteness matches the following qualifier, and the shared -atin cadence with tanwīn liaison makes life and satisfaction sound like one state-unit. Lexically it is not bare existence; the {{ar:ع ي ش}} ({{tr:'-y-sh}}) range names lived condition and can carry livelihood or subsistence texture, so the reward feels experiential and provisioned rather than abstract. Its pattern and indefiniteness make that life both specific and open: a particular mode of living, yet not delimited as a named or exhausted object. The exact phrase recurs at 69:21, where the right-hand record leads to the same reward formula, while 101:7 specializes the formula through heavy scales. In the same surah, the later opposite at 101:9 makes this life-state the reward-side abode image against a falling-abode outcome.

words.prose: {{ar:رَّاضِيَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:rāḍiyatin}}) seals the ayah by making satisfaction the final quality of the reward scene. Its feminine genitive indefinite agreement ties it to {{ar:عِيشَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:'īshatin}}), not to the masculine pronoun, so the life-state itself is the bearer of contentment. The active participle is crucial: it presents the life as satisfied from within, not as something merely approved by an outside evaluator. That active/passive distinction is made explicit by the paired forms in 89:28, while 101:7 selects only the active side. The word also participates in the exact reward phrase repeated at 69:21, so the final adjective is both a local grammatical closure and a recognizable reward marker. The liaison from the preceding tanwīn fuses the qualifier into the life phrase, and the emphatic ḍ gives the final satisfaction a dense center; together, sound and position let the moral heaviness of 101:6 settle into contentment at the ayah's last word.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction fahuwa fi places the person inside ʿishah, while the feminine active descriptor radiyah grammatically makes the lived condition itself the bearer of satisfaction.
baseline_models.mechanism: Containment and personification combine: the subject does not merely possess a reward but inhabits a whole condition of living from which displeasure is absent.

activation_trace.role: Life and lived condition supplies the encompassing state in which the person is placed.
Acceptance opposed to displeasure gives that encompassing life its affective quality.

changed_reading.before: He will have a pleasant life.
changed_reading.after: He is enclosed within a lived condition that is itself satisfied and free of aversion.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The noun ʿishah can name not only life in the abstract but the means, provisions, and place by which living is sustained.
baseline_models.mechanism: The phrase can describe an ecology of subsistence: food, drink, place, and support cohere as an acceptable livelihood rather than serving as decorative pleasures around an otherwise unchanged subject.

activation_trace.role: Livelihood, provision, and place of living turn ʿishah into a sustaining environment.
The non-dominant mapped inventory's acceptance sense marks the sustaining environment as fully acceptable.

changed_reading.before: The verse promises a generically happy existence.
changed_reading.after: The verse places him within a satisfactory means-and-place of living whose supports are part of the gift.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Because radiyah agrees with ʿishah, the wording leaves the life grammatically active rather than stating only that its human inhabitant is pleased.
baseline_models.mechanism: The mutual-consent branch activates a bilateral relation: the person fits the life and the life, personified, accepts its inhabitant. This coexists with the simpler idiom of a pleasing life.

activation_trace.role: The lived condition provides one side of a relation rather than merely an inert possession.
Mutual consent supplies the image of reciprocal accord between the life and its inhabitant.

changed_reading.before: The person likes the life awarded to him.
changed_reading.after: Person and lived condition are in reciprocal fit: he is at home in it, and it is figured as accepting him.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated impact and exposure make the focus preposition fi newly salient. Against a world struck open or emptied, being inside a life reads as recovered enclosure and continuity after rupture.

activation_trace.role: The whole lived condition is the enclosure whose force changes under the impact cue.
One thing striking another supplies the initiating rupture against which enclosure matters.
Uncovering and emptiness sharpen the contrast between exposure and being held within a life.

structural_cues: The same event-name occupies 101:1, 101:2, and 101:3 before the focus result begins with fa and locates its subject with fi.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated striking and uncovering plus the focus's inside-construction; I infer a rupture-to-enclosure contrast, not that q-r-ʿ lexically means loss of shelter. A live alternative is simple temporal contrast after the event.

changed_reading.before: The life is a static pleasant reward.
changed_reading.after: The life is also a post-impact enclosure: a condition able to hold its inhabitant after ordinary structures have been struck open.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated challenge of knowing brackets the outcomes, while the focus uses interior location and an evaluative adjective. Satisfaction can therefore function as knowledge available from inhabiting the condition, not as an external inventory of its contents.

activation_trace.role: A lived condition is something encountered from within, supporting experiential rather than merely propositional knowledge.
Acceptance supplies the condition's internally registered verdict.
Knowledge and discernment open an epistemic gap before the scene is disclosed.
The repeated knowledge challenge near the opposite outcome makes the focus's compressed qualitative report conspicuous.

structural_cues: The formula asking what could make the addressee know appears before the transformations and again before the final identification, whereas 101:7 names only an inhabited quality.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit knowledge challenges and an interior life-description; I infer that radiyah can act as an experiential disclosure. It may instead be only concise reward language, so the epistemic function remains contextual rather than lexical.

changed_reading.before: Radiyah is a vague synonym for pleasant.
changed_reading.after: Radiyah is the inside verdict of the life: its adequacy is known in being lived even though its contents are not itemized.

context_deltas.mechanism: A bounded event-time in which radical transformations come to be opens into an inhabited life-state. The focus thus reads as a new regime generated by the event rather than as a continuation of ordinary biological life.

activation_trace.role: Life and lived condition supplies the abiding regime reached after the event.
A delimited duration frames the transformations as an event phase.
Coming to presence in time supplies the transition from event to newly actualized condition.

structural_cues: Yawm yakunu introduces what people become, then 101:6-7 moves through evaluation to fahuwa fi, a result expressed as stable location.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies event-time, coming-to-be, and an inhabited life; I infer a phase transition from bounded upheaval into an abiding regime. The alternative is that yawm merely dates an otherwise conventional reward.

changed_reading.before: ʿIshah is ordinary life made more pleasant.
changed_reading.after: ʿIshah is a newly actualized mode of living on the far side of the event's transformations.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context dismantles coherence in parallel social and material domains: familiar humans lose gathering and companionship, while solid terrain becomes light, soft, and expanded. The focus life can therefore be heard as the counter-state in which social and material supports again cohere into habitability.

activation_trace.role: Means, provisions, and place of living provide the habitat whose coherence is at stake.
Human companionship that removes estrangement supplies the social coherence lost in the scene.
The light flying creature supplies unstable, directionless mobility for the human collective.
Scattering converts the collective into separated units and breaks social containment.
Elevated solid aggregation supplies the material coherence that is being undone.
Softening and breakage without clean separation turns firmness into yielding fibers.
Fluffed expansion completes the loss of compact material support.

structural_cues: Two consecutive similes transform people and mountains in parallel before the two outcome clauses restore sharply differentiated destinations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies social scattering and material decompaction; I infer that a means-and-place of living answers both losses by restoring coherence. A weaker alternative is that the chaos serves only as backdrop for generic comfort.

changed_reading.before: The good outcome is private emotional comfort.
changed_reading.after: The good outcome is an inhabitable order: social belonging and material support cohere again around the person.

context_deltas.mechanism: Weight carries worth, and weighing carries justice. Because the focus follows as the direct fa-result, satisfaction becomes an accepted settlement produced by valuation, not an arbitrary sensation or decorative luxury.

activation_trace.role: The lived condition is the settlement assigned by the evaluative process.
Acceptance from the non-dominant mapped inventory makes radiyah sound like ratification as well as pleasure.
Precious weight turns heaviness into worth rather than mere physical load.
The balance of justice supplies the normative procedure that yields the accepted life.
Weight as standing or rank makes the outcome answer demonstrated value.

structural_cues: 101:6 gives the condition and 101:7 begins with fa, making the inhabited life the immediate consequence of heavy balances.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies worth, just weighing, rank, and a grammatical result; I infer that acceptance is the verdict embodied as a life. Pleasure remains a live concomitant, but it no longer exhausts radiyah.

changed_reading.before: The person receives a pleasant reward after being weighed.
changed_reading.after: He enters a life that embodies a just, accepted verdict—its satisfaction is also ratification of the measured worth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The balance can be an alignment between two things, while the focus inventory allows mutual satisfaction. Together they activate a fit model in which person and life are brought into proportion rather than pleasure flowing only one way.

activation_trace.role: The concrete supports and place of living form one side of the fit.
Mutual consent makes satisfaction bilateral rather than a one-way reaction.
Balancing and aligning two things supplies the mechanism of proportional fit.

structural_cues: The weighing clause and the life clause are joined as condition and consequence, while radiyah agrees with the life rather than directly predicating contentment of the person.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies alignment and mutual consent; I map physical balance onto relational congruence. The live alternative is ordinary measurement followed by a unilaterally pleasing reward.

changed_reading.before: A favorable measurement purchases pleasures for the person.
changed_reading.after: The measurement places him in a mode of life proportioned to him, with reciprocal accord between inhabitant and habitat.

context_deltas.mechanism: The paired weight outcomes lead to opposed receiving environments. Lightness culminates in an origin-or-return figured as a falling abyss; by contrast, being fi ʿishah becomes arrival in a stable, sustaining home-world.

activation_trace.role: Means and place of living let the positive destination function as a sustaining home.
The repeated balance sets the two destinations into direct structural comparison.
Lightness of load supplies the failed counterweight that opens the opposite trajectory.
Origin, gathering point, and return turn the negative destination into a perverse home or receiving matrix.
Falling into a depth gives the opposite home its irreversible downward motion.

structural_cues: The fa-amma and wa-amma alternatives mirror each other; the positive says fahuwa fi, while the negative answers with fa-ummuhu, making both outcomes forms of reception.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies paired balances, an inside-position, a root of origin and return, and falling; I infer that both outcomes are destination-environments. The maternal force of umm may remain metaphorical rather than defining every nuance of the contrast.

changed_reading.before: One outcome is happiness and the other is punishment.
changed_reading.after: The weighing routes each person to a counterhome: one receives and sustains life, while the other receives by letting its inhabitant fall.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opposite destination is personified through maternal language, while the focus life is already grammatically capable of satisfaction. The contrast activates a relational host model: the good life does not merely contain goods but receives, sustains, and accords with its inhabitant.

activation_trace.role: Provision and place of living provide the sustaining functions of the positive host.
Mutual consent allows the host-life and inhabitant to be figured in reciprocal accord.
The mother as bearer and nurturer supplies the relational hosting pattern, inverted by the abyss.
The falling depth makes the negative host anti-nurturing and sharpens the positive reversal.

structural_cues: Both outcome clauses personify what receives the person: a satisfied life in 101:7 and an abyss named through umm in 101:9.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies maternal nurture, a falling destination, livelihood support, and mutual accord; I infer a positive host by contrast with the anti-maternal abyss. The alternative retains umm as a conventional destination metaphor without projecting maternal qualities onto ʿishah.

changed_reading.before: The person is pleased by objects located in the good life.
changed_reading.after: The life-world itself receives and sustains him, and its being radiyah figures a living accord with the one it hosts.

context_deltas.mechanism: The negative outcome is eventually exposed through concrete fire and heat, whereas the positive outcome remains a compressed inhabited quality. This asymmetry lets radiyah serve not as vagueness but as a sufficient disclosure: acceptability characterizes the life as a whole without a catalog.

activation_trace.role: The whole lived condition is summarized qualitatively rather than decomposed into separate rewards.
Acceptance opposed to displeasure operates as the positive condition's complete evaluative seal.
Kindled fire gives the opposite outcome a concrete destructive substance.
Heat completes the materially explicit disclosure against which the positive compression stands.

structural_cues: The positive result is one compact prepositional phrase; the negative result receives a renewed knowledge question and then a two-word material identification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rhetorical asymmetry, fire, heat, and the focus's whole-life adjective; I infer that radiyah intentionally gives a total verdict rather than an incomplete picture. A live alternative is simple stylistic compression with no epistemic contrast.

changed_reading.before: The positive outcome is underspecified compared with the fire.
changed_reading.after: Its non-catalog form is meaningful: the entire lived condition is disclosed as acceptable, while the opposite must be exposed by its consuming material.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it joins two rare guarantee branches and the radiyy descriptor is form-distant from radiyah here. It remains anchored in the focus noun's livelihood sense and adjective root, with a context branch independently supplying standing surety; downstream prose should call it a functional echo, not a lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ʿIshah can denote the means by which life continues, and the non-dominant r-d-y inventory includes a descriptor associated with guaranteeing.

activation_trace.role: Livelihood and subsistence provide what must be maintained or guaranteed.
The form-distant descriptor of obedience, love, or guarantee activates a surety-like quality in radiyah.
Guaranteeing and standing over another supplies an independent support relation that keeps the activation live.

changed_reading.before: The life is merely enjoyable while it lasts.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it is a livelihood that stands surety for its inhabitant—a sustaining condition whose continuance is secured.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because drawing lots and being selected are remote branches of the repeated event-name, not the obvious force of its surface occurrence. It remains anchored in the focus's fa-marked assignment to a life and is reinforced by just weighing; downstream prose should present it only as an allotment-pattern activated across the sequence.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Fahuwa makes the person the recipient of a resultant placement, and fi ʿishah names the condition into which he is placed.

activation_trace.role: The lived condition supplies the allotment or placement produced by the sequence.
Drawing lots supplies the remote image of differentiating and assigning outcomes.
Being picked or chosen sharpens the event's remote selection pattern.
Just balance constrains the selection image by making the resultant placement adjudicated rather than random.

changed_reading.before: The good life simply follows the event.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the event sorts and the balance adjudicates, so the satisfied life reads as the person's selected allotment.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the protection branch shares the root of the surface adjective describing intense heat, so the reversal is cross-branch rather than the clause's direct sense. It remains anchored in fi plus the focus livelihood/place branch and in the final root's supplied protection image; downstream prose should mark it as a contrastive affordance, not claim that hamiyah means protective here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Being fi a means-and-place of living permits the positive life to be read as an enclosure with a sustaining function.

activation_trace.role: Place and means of living anchor the positive side as a sustaining enclosure.
Absence of displeasure marks the enclosure as hospitable rather than hostile.
Kindled fire supplies the hostile enclosure against which the focus is reversed.
Protection and prevention activate the latent opposite affordance of a boundary: shelter rather than consuming confinement.

changed_reading.before: The focus and final fire are merely unrelated reward and punishment images.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they are opposed enclosures: the satisfied life sustains and shelters, while the fiery depth encloses by consuming.

strongest_changes: The phrase shifts from generic pleasure to a whole lived condition that is itself figured as satisfied.
Heavy, just balances make that condition an accepted verdict embodied as life.
The paired outcomes turn ʿishah into a sustaining counterhome to the light-weighted fall into an abyss.
The scattering of people and loosening of mountains makes the good life a reconstituted social and material habitat.
summary.what_was_special: The focus adjective remains productively active: context does not force a single gloss but lets life appear at once as verdict, habitat, reciprocal partner, and receiving home. Remote guarantee, allotment, and protection branches add contained exploratory readings without displacing the stronger models.
remaining_uncertainties: The grammar keeps open how strongly radiyah personifies the life as satisfied, rather than idiomatically describing it as pleasing.
ʿIshah can foreground lived condition or concrete livelihood and habitat; the context supports both without settling their proportion.
The guarantee, selection, maternal-host, and protective-reversal mechanisms depend on abductive cross-branch arrows and should remain explicitly qualified.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. Life as condition matched to weight. Evidence: ع ي ش B001, life and lived condition; ر ض و B001, acceptance opposed to displeasure; و ز ن B002/B007 in 101:6, just balance and valued standing. Structural cue: فَهُوَ marks direct consequence after ثقلت موازينه. Mechanism: adjudicated worth produces an inhabited condition that itself is accepting/accepted. Abductive move: I infer that the life is not merely pleasant but congruent with the scale's judgment. Reading change: عيشة راضية reads as an environment aligned with justice.

2. Livelihood after stripped provisions. Evidence: ع ي ش B002, means of living/livelihood; ع ه ن B001 in 101:5, ready accessible property/food/drink; ف ر ش B002, prepared resting place. Structural cue: after worldly supports are scattered/fluffed, this ayah supplies a new "in" space. Mechanism: the rewarded person receives not only survival but a complete provision-place. Abductive move: I supply replacement: collapsed earthly provisioning is answered by a different livelihood. Reading change: عيشة is read materially as sustaining habitation, not only abstract life.

3. Mutual consent/restored relation. Evidence: ر ض و B003, reciprocal satisfaction; ر ض و B004, making another satisfied; ر ح م B002 at 101:0, kinship bond. Structural cue: the singular "he" enters a feminized عيشة راضية after the communal chaos of الناس. Mechanism: isolated judgment is reabsorbed into a relation of acceptance and care. Abductive move: I infer social/affective repair from رضى branches and the opening kinship field. Reading change: the ayah reads as reconciled belonging rather than solitary reward.

4. Obedient/guaranteeing life. Evidence: ر ض و B006, raḍiyy as obedient, loving, or guaranteeing; ك و ن B003, suretyship/responsibility; ث ق ل B005, precious protected worth. Structural cue: the life follows a successful scale result. Mechanism: the new life acts almost as guarantor for the one whose weight was accepted. Abductive move: I supply a juridical protection relation from "guaranteeing" to the rewarded state. Reading change: راضية can be heard as a life that receives, loves, and secures its inhabitant.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: 101:9 retrospectively made the relational language of عيشة راضية stronger: the bad outcome also has a feminine receiving-place, but as mother/abyss. 101:11 clarified that the good "in a life" contrasts with being enclosed in a heated zone.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The life-condition itself is the satisfied subject.** `ع ي ش B001` includes life and the quality of a lived condition, while `ر ض و B001` includes active acceptance opposed to displeasure. Grammatically, the feminine active adjective `رَّاضِيَةٍ` agrees with `عِيشَةٍ`; the condition, not an explicitly named inhabitant, bears satisfaction. The branch role is personification of a life that accepts or fits the person delivered to it by `فَهُوَ`. I infer that grammatical agency signals suitability rather than literal emotion. The ayah reads as congruence between person and condition, not merely private pleasure within it.

2. **Balance becomes reciprocal fit.** `ر ض و B003` supplies satisfaction by mutual consent. The heavy balances of 101:6 and the locative relation `فِى عِيشَةٍ` place evaluated person and resulting life in relation; the active adjective lets satisfaction point back from the condition toward its inhabitant. The branch's role is reciprocity: the person receives the life, and the life is presented as accepting the person. This mutuality is inferred because the fixed form is not morphologically reciprocal. It adds a relational outcome to the judicial mechanism rather than reducing reward to possession.

3. **Life as a sustaining habitat.** `ع ي ش B002` covers livelihood, provisions, and the means or place by which one lives. The preposition `فِى` frames `عِيشَةٍ` as an encompassing condition. Later, 101:9-11 also gives the opposed person an encompassing destination, first as `أُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ` and then as fire. This spatial opposition assigns the livelihood branch the role of a sustaining environment. I infer that the two outcomes are structurally comparable habitats; the text does not repeat `فِى` in the negative clause. The ayah thus describes entry into a life-supporting order, not a passing feeling.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The negative sequence in 101:8-11 retrospectively changed the force of `فِى`. The opposed person is re-centered in a mother/abyss and that referent is identified as fire, so `ع ي ش B002` becomes an inhabitable, sustaining environment by contrast. This also sharpened the exploratory `ر ض و B003` reading: the positive condition fits its inhabitant, whereas the negative enclosure receives without mutual satisfaction.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, yaşamın kendisini ve özellikle canlılara özgü yaşama durumunu temel anlam olarak verir; ayrıca bu yaşamın iyi, hoşnut edici, övgüye değer, kötü ya da dar ve sıkıntılı oluşunu belirtir. lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın kullanım yaşamın kendisini belirtir; iyi, kötü, hoşnut edici ya da sıkıntılı oluş gibi nitelikler ise belirli biçim ve söz öbeklerine bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Canlıların sürdürdüğü yaşamın kendisini ve bu yaşamın iyi, hoşnut edici, övgüye değer, kötü ya da dar ve sıkıntılı oluşunu belirtir. Ayrıca iyi durumda yaşayan kimseyi niteleyen bağlı bir kullanımı kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, canlı olma ve yaşamı sürdürme olgusu olarak yaşamın kendisidir.
Yaşayışın iyi, hoşnut edici, övgüye değer, kötü veya dar ve sıkıntılı oluşu belirli nitelemelerle anlatılır.
İyi durumda yaşayan kimse, yaşayışının elverişli oluşuna dayanılarak nitelenebilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yaşamın kendisi ile bu yaşamın iyi, kötü, hoşnut edici veya sıkıntılı oluşunu birlikte temsil eden en geniş doğal karşılıktır.

Tanrı-kul ilişkisinde aynı çekirdek, taraflara göre hükme karşı çıkmama ve buyruğa uygun davranışı onaylama biçiminde ayrışır.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

source_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

branch_policy.compact_gloss_policy: Reviewed gloss branches remain as branch_ref/payload_tier stubs; their branch records are trimmed, not filtered out.
branch_policy.note: Every root target and dictionary branch identity is retained. Branch payload detail is tiered from generation-time citations; non-full branches and reviewed gloss records are trimmed, not absent. Root lexicon and branch inventory availability never create interest.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
